question.text: How should you scan while driving on the highway, and what should you do before studying a map?

answer.text: Keep scanning ahead, to the sides and behind, and never look away from the road for more than a few seconds; to study a map, first pull safely off the road.

teaching.text: Never look away from the road for more than a few seconds, and pull safely off the road before studying a map. Remember: eyes moving, map off road.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep scanning ahead, to the sides and behind, and never look away from the road for more than a few seconds; to study a map, first pull safely off the road.

question.text: On a highway with one lane each way, which lane do you use, and when may you cross the center line to pass?

answer.text: On a highway with one lane each way, drive in the right lane, crossing the center line to pass only when no oncoming vehicle is near and there is no solid yellow line.

teaching.text: The right lane is the travel lane; cross the center line to pass only with no oncoming vehicle near and no solid yellow line. Remember: right lane, careful pass.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a highway with one lane each way, drive in the right lane, crossing the center line to pass only when no oncoming vehicle is near and there is no solid yellow line.

question.text: On a highway with two or more lanes each way, when may you leave the right lane?

answer.text: On a highway with two or more lanes each way, stay right except to pass slower traffic, make room for a merging driver, or set up a legal left turn.

teaching.text: On two or more lanes each way, leave the right lane only to pass, make room for a merging driver or set up a left turn. Remember: keep right except passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a highway with two or more lanes each way, stay right except to pass slower traffic, make room for a merging driver, or set up a legal left turn.

question.text: How does lane use differ between a two-lane highway and one with four or more lanes?

answer.text: On a two-lane highway the right lane is the travel lane and the center line may be crossed to pass, while on four or more lanes you keep right except for passing, merging room or a left turn.

teaching.text: Identify the road first: two lanes allow crossing the center line to pass, while wider highways keep you right with exceptions. Remember: two lanes versus four.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a two-lane highway the right lane is the travel lane and the center line may be crossed to pass, while on four or more lanes you keep right except for passing, merging room or a left turn.

question.text: How do you control your speed, especially after leaving a fast road?

answer.text: Control your speed by checking the speedometer often and watching posted limits, especially after leaving a fast road for much slower local streets.

teaching.text: Speed is easy to misjudge after a fast stretch, so check the speedometer often on slower local streets. Remember: watch the speedometer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Control your speed by checking the speedometer often and watching posted limits, especially after leaving a fast road for much slower local streets.

question.text: Which lanes may be used for passing, and which part of the road may never be used?

answer.text: The left lane is for passing only, the right lane may be used to pass a vehicle turning left, and the shoulder or unpaved edge must never be used for passing.

teaching.text: The left lane is for passing, the right lane may be used to pass a left-turning vehicle, and the shoulder never. Remember: never pass on shoulders.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The left lane is for passing only, the right lane may be used to pass a vehicle turning left, and the shoulder or unpaved edge must never be used for passing.

question.text: What checks do you make before passing on a four-lane highway?

answer.text: Before passing on a four-lane highway, check the left lane with your left and inside mirrors and take a quick look over your left shoulder.

teaching.text: Use the left and inside mirrors, then look over your left shoulder before moving out to pass. Remember: mirrors plus left shoulder.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before passing on a four-lane highway, check the left lane with your left and inside mirrors and take a quick look over your left shoulder.

question.text: What is a blind spot, and why is a shoulder check needed?

answer.text: A blind spot is an area your rearview mirrors cannot show, which is why a glance over the shoulder is needed before changing lanes.

teaching.text: Mirrors cannot show a blind spot, which is why a glance over the shoulder comes before a lane change. Remember: mirrors miss it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A blind spot is an area your rearview mirrors cannot show, which is why a glance over the shoulder is needed before changing lanes.

question.text: Where should you avoid riding near another vehicle, and what do you do instead?

answer.text: Avoid riding just behind and to either side of another vehicle; speed up or drop back so its driver can see you.

teaching.text: Riding just behind and to the side of a car hides you from its driver, so speed up or drop back. Remember: be seen, not hidden.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Avoid riding just behind and to either side of another vehicle; speed up or drop back so its driver can see you.

question.text: How should you move through another driver's blind spot when passing?

answer.text: When passing, move through the other driver's blind spot as fast as you can without going over the speed limit.

teaching.text: Move through the blind spot quickly within the speed limit, because lingering there raises the risk of a collision. Remember: through the blind spot briskly.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When passing, move through the other driver's blind spot as fast as you can without going over the speed limit.

question.text: What is the risk of staying in another driver's blind spot while passing?

answer.text: The longer you stay in another driver's blind spot while passing, the longer you risk that vehicle moving into yours.

teaching.text: The longer you stay in another driver's blind spot, the longer that vehicle might move into yours. Remember: linger, risk a merge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The longer you stay in another driver's blind spot while passing, the longer you risk that vehicle moving into yours.

question.text: Why should you not linger beside or behind a truck or bus?

answer.text: Do not linger beside or right behind a truck or bus, whose large blind spots hide you; if the trucker's face is not visible in the side mirror, you are not visible to the trucker.

teaching.text: If you cannot see the trucker's face in the side mirror, the trucker cannot see you. Remember: no face, no view.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not linger beside or right behind a truck or bus, whose large blind spots hide you; if the trucker's face is not visible in the side mirror, you are not visible to the trucker.

question.text: After passing a truck, when do you return to the lane, and what do you avoid?

answer.text: After passing a truck, wait until its cab appears in your rearview mirror before returning to the lane, keep your speed, and do not slow down in front of it.

teaching.text: Wait until the truck's cab appears in your mirror before returning, and do not slow down in front of it. Remember: see the cab first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After passing a truck, wait until its cab appears in your rearview mirror before returning to the lane, keep your speed, and do not slow down in front of it.

question.text: If the way is clear, how do you make the pass?

answer.text: If the way is clear, signal the lane change, then pass quickly and smoothly without exceeding the limit.

teaching.text: Signal the lane change, then make the pass quickly and smoothly without exceeding the limit. Remember: signal, pass smoothly.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the way is clear, signal the lane change, then pass quickly and smoothly without exceeding the limit.

question.text: When may you return to the right lane after passing?

answer.text: Return to the right lane only once the passed vehicle shows in your rearview mirror, after a look over your right shoulder and a signal.

teaching.text: Return only once the passed vehicle shows in your rearview mirror, after a right shoulder look and a signal. Remember: mirror, shoulder, signal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Return to the right lane only once the passed vehicle shows in your rearview mirror, after a look over your right shoulder and a signal.

question.text: Which shoulder do you check before moving out to pass, and which before moving back in?

answer.text: The shoulder check flips with the direction of the lane change: before moving out to pass you look over the left shoulder, and before moving back in you look over the right one.

teaching.text: Look left before moving out and right before moving back in. Remember: left out, right back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The shoulder check flips with the direction of the lane change: before moving out to pass you look over the left shoulder, and before moving back in you look over the right one.

question.text: What should you do when someone starts to pass you?

answer.text: When someone starts to pass you, hold your lane and do not speed up.

teaching.text: Holding your lane and speed lets the passing driver finish quickly and safely. Remember: hold lane, hold speed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When someone starts to pass you, hold your lane and do not speed up.

question.text: What does it mean if many drivers pass you on the right on a multi-lane road?

answer.text: If many drivers are passing you on the right in a multi-lane road, you are likely slower than traffic and should move right when clear unless a left turn is coming up.

teaching.text: Being passed on the right by many drivers means you are likely slower than traffic, so move right when clear. Remember: passed on the right, move right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If many drivers are passing you on the right in a multi-lane road, you are likely slower than traffic and should move right when clear unless a left turn is coming up.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: passed on the right, move right

question.text: Why should you keep pace with traffic?

answer.text: Crashes involving two or more vehicles often happen when one driver goes faster or slower than the others, so keep pace with traffic.

teaching.text: Many multi-vehicle crashes involve one driver going faster or slower than the rest of traffic. Remember: match the flow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Crashes involving two or more vehicles often happen when one driver goes faster or slower than the others, so keep pace with traffic.

question.text: What does speeding really gain you, and what does each pass add?

answer.text: Speeding saves no more than a few minutes an hour, and each pass you make adds another chance of a collision.

teaching.text: Speeding saves only a few minutes an hour, and every extra pass adds another chance of a collision. Remember: minutes saved, risk added.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Speeding saves no more than a few minutes an hour, and each pass you make adds another chance of a collision.

question.text: What should you do if a line of vehicles builds up behind you?

answer.text: Driving much slower than traffic is also dangerous; if a line of vehicles builds behind you, pull over when safe and let them by.

teaching.text: A slow car with a line behind it should pull over when safe and let the vehicles pass. Remember: pull over, let them by.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driving much slower than traffic is also dangerous; if a line of vehicles builds behind you, pull over when safe and let them by.

question.text: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?

answer.text: Check your rearview mirrors every few seconds to track traffic coming up behind you.

teaching.text: Checking your mirrors every few seconds keeps track of traffic coming up behind you. Remember: mirrors every few seconds.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Check your rearview mirrors every few seconds to track traffic coming up behind you.

question.text: Why should you spot slow vehicles early?

answer.text: Spot slow vehicles early, such as heavy trucks and underpowered cars on steep grades or merging, so you can change lanes or ease off instead of braking suddenly.

teaching.text: Spotting slow trucks and underpowered cars early lets you change lanes or ease off instead of braking hard. Remember: see slow traffic early.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Spot slow vehicles early, such as heavy trucks and underpowered cars on steep grades or merging, so you can change lanes or ease off instead of braking suddenly.

question.text: Which vehicles may lose speed on climbs and need extra time to join traffic?

answer.text: Slow trucks and small underpowered vehicles may lose speed on long or steep climbs and need extra time to get up to speed when they join traffic.

teaching.text: Slow trucks and small underpowered vehicles may lose speed on long climbs and need extra time to join traffic. Remember: heavy and underpowered vehicles.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Slow trucks and small underpowered vehicles may lose speed on long or steep climbs and need extra time to get up to speed when they join traffic.

question.text: How should you set your following distance on the highway?

answer.text: Keep a safe following distance from the vehicle ahead, using the spacing method in the everyday driving chapter.

teaching.text: Use the spacing method from the everyday driving chapter to keep a safe following distance. Remember: use the spacing method.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep a safe following distance from the vehicle ahead, using the spacing method in the everyday driving chapter.

question.text: Where should you never stop on a highway, and where should you stop instead?

answer.text: Never stop in the travel lanes of a highway; use rest stops and service areas instead.

teaching.text: Never stop in a highway travel lane; rest stops and service areas are the places to stop. Remember: rest stops, not lanes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never stop in the travel lanes of a highway; use rest stops and service areas instead.

question.text: Why should you look far enough ahead to avoid panic stops?

answer.text: Look far enough ahead to avoid panic stops, because hard braking can cost you control and makes it harder for drivers behind to stop.

teaching.text: Hard braking can cost you control, so look far enough ahead to slow down gradually. Remember: far eyes, soft stops.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Look far enough ahead to avoid panic stops, because hard braking can cost you control and makes it harder for drivers behind to stop.

question.text: What can slowing or changing lanes early do for you?

answer.text: Slowing or changing lanes early may let you avoid stopping entirely, and any stop you do make will be more gradual and safer.

teaching.text: Slowing or changing lanes early may let you avoid a stop entirely, and any stop will be gentler. Remember: early moves, gentle stops.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Slowing or changing lanes early may let you avoid stopping entirely, and any stop you do make will be more gradual and safer.

question.text: How do you get on and off a controlled access highway?

answer.text: A controlled access highway lets you get on or off only at entrance and exit ramps.

teaching.text: A controlled access highway can be entered and left only at ramps. Remember: ramps only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A controlled access highway lets you get on or off only at entrance and exit ramps.

question.text: Which way does traffic move on entrance and exit ramps?

answer.text: Entrance ramps and exit ramps are both short ramps that carry traffic in one direction only.

teaching.text: Entrance and exit ramps are short and carry traffic in one direction only. Remember: ramps run one way.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Entrance ramps and exit ramps are both short ramps that carry traffic in one direction only.

question.text: How do you use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane?

answer.text: Use the entrance ramp and its acceleration lane to reach the speed of highway traffic, then signal and merge smoothly into a gap.

teaching.text: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of highway traffic before signaling and merging into a gap. Remember: speed up, then merge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Use the entrance ramp and its acceleration lane to reach the speed of highway traffic, then signal and merge smoothly into a gap.

question.text: When is stopping at the end of the acceleration lane acceptable?

answer.text: Stopping where the acceleration lane ends is only for very heavy traffic that leaves you no choice.

teaching.text: Stopping at the end of the acceleration lane is only for very heavy traffic that leaves no choice. Remember: only in heavy traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Stopping where the acceleration lane ends is only for very heavy traffic that leaves you no choice.

question.text: What if highway drivers do not make room for you to merge?

answer.text: Drivers on the highway should make room for you, but if they do not, you must yield to them rather than force your way in, even if that means stopping.

teaching.text: Highway drivers should make room, but if they do not, you yield rather than force your way in. Remember: yield, do not force.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers on the highway should make room for you, but if they do not, you must yield to them rather than force your way in, even if that means stopping.

question.text: How do you leave a highway using the deceleration lane?

answer.text: Move into the correct lane well before the deceleration lane, then use that lane and the exit ramp to slow down, obeying the ramp's advisory speed sign.

teaching.text: Get into the correct lane early, then slow down in the deceleration lane and on the ramp, obeying its advisory speed. Remember: early lane, slow ramp.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Move into the correct lane well before the deceleration lane, then use that lane and the exit ramp to slow down, obeying the ramp's advisory speed sign.

question.text: Where are the acceleration and deceleration lanes, and what is each for?

answer.text: An acceleration lane sits at the end of most entrance ramps and is for speeding up, while a deceleration lane sits at the start of most exit ramps and is for slowing down.

teaching.text: The acceleration lane ends the entrance ramp for speeding up; the deceleration lane starts the exit ramp for slowing down. Remember: speed up in, slow down out.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An acceleration lane sits at the end of most entrance ramps and is for speeding up, while a deceleration lane sits at the start of most exit ramps and is for slowing down.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: speed up in, slow down out

question.text: What should you do if you miss your exit?

answer.text: If you miss your exit, never stop, back up or turn around on the highway; take the next exit and come back.

teaching.text: If you miss your exit, never stop, back up or turn around on the highway; take the next exit. Remember: next exit, come back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you miss your exit, never stop, back up or turn around on the highway; take the next exit and come back.

question.text: What is an interchange?

answer.text: An interchange is where two busy highways meet using entrance and exit ramps, and it can be confusing the first time you use it.

teaching.text: An interchange is where two busy highways meet using ramps, and it can be confusing the first time. Remember: where highways meet.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An interchange is where two busy highways meet using entrance and exit ramps, and it can be confusing the first time you use it.

question.text: What four common interchange layouts does the guide name?

answer.text: The guide pictures four common interchange layouts: cloverleaf, diamond, directional and diverging diamond.

teaching.text: The four common layouts are the cloverleaf, the diamond, the directional and the diverging diamond. Remember: cloverleaf, diamond, directional, diverging.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The guide pictures four common interchange layouts: cloverleaf, diamond, directional and diverging diamond.

question.text: What is different about driving through a Diverging Diamond Interchange?

answer.text: On a Diverging Diamond Interchange you drive on the left side of the road for a short stretch, and directional signs at every interchange help you find your way.

teaching.text: On a diverging diamond you drive on the left side for a short stretch, and directional signs guide you. Remember: briefly on the left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a Diverging Diamond Interchange you drive on the left side of the road for a short stretch, and directional signs at every interchange help you find your way.

question.text: What is highway hypnosis?

answer.text: Highway hypnosis is a drowsy, unaware state caused by the sameness of the road and traffic and the steady hum of wind, tires and engine.

teaching.text: Highway hypnosis comes from the sameness of the road and the steady hum of the car. Remember: sameness lulls you.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Highway hypnosis is a drowsy, unaware state caused by the sameness of the road and traffic and the steady hum of wind, tires and engine.

question.text: How do you prevent highway hypnosis?

answer.text: Prevent highway hypnosis by keeping your eyes moving over traffic and signs, and leave the highway if you start to feel sleepy.

teaching.text: Keep your eyes moving over traffic and signs, and leave the highway if you start to feel sleepy. Remember: eyes moving, exit if sleepy.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Prevent highway hypnosis by keeping your eyes moving over traffic and signs, and leave the highway if you start to feel sleepy.

question.text: Why is drowsy driving dangerous, and what should a very sleepy driver do?

answer.text: A drowsy driver decides and reacts more slowly and can be as dangerous as a drunk one, so stop at the nearest rest area or service area and nap if very sleepy.

teaching.text: A drowsy driver reacts more slowly and can be as dangerous as a drunk one, so stop and nap if very sleepy. Remember: drowsy like drunk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A drowsy driver decides and reacts more slowly and can be as dangerous as a drunk one, so stop at the nearest rest area or service area and nap if very sleepy.

question.text: What single fix does the guide give for highway hypnosis and sleepiness?

answer.text: Highway hypnosis and plain sleepiness share one fix in the guide: get off the highway rather than risk falling asleep at the wheel.

teaching.text: For both highway hypnosis and sleepiness, the fix is to get off the highway rather than risk falling asleep. Remember: get off the highway.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Highway hypnosis and plain sleepiness share one fix in the guide: get off the highway rather than risk falling asleep at the wheel.

question.text: Why do many crashes happen, and what does the guide advise?

answer.text: Many crashes happen because drivers do not give enough attention to driving, so stay alert for unexpected events.

teaching.text: Many crashes come from not paying enough attention to driving, so stay alert for the unexpected. Remember: attention prevents crashes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Many crashes happen because drivers do not give enough attention to driving, so stay alert for unexpected events.

question.text: Where may you stop in an emergency, and what signals help?

answer.text: In an emergency you may stop on the shoulder; turn on your emergency flashers, and raising the hood or tying a white cloth to the antenna also helps.

teaching.text: You may stop on the shoulder in an emergency, with flashers on and the hood raised or a white cloth tied on. Remember: shoulder, flashers, hood.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In an emergency you may stop on the shoulder; turn on your emergency flashers, and raising the hood or tying a white cloth to the antenna also helps.

question.text: Which signals does the guide suggest for an emergency stop on the shoulder?

answer.text: A white cloth on the antenna and a raised hood are the signals suggested for an emergency stop on the shoulder, together with emergency flashers.

teaching.text: Emergency flashers, a raised hood and a white cloth on the antenna are the suggested signals for a shoulder stop. Remember: hood up, white cloth.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A white cloth on the antenna and a raised hood are the signals suggested for an emergency stop on the shoulder, together with emergency flashers.

question.text: Why must other drivers be able to see you after a breakdown?

answer.text: After a breakdown, make sure other drivers can see you and your vehicle, since crashes happen when a stalled car is noticed too late.

teaching.text: A stalled car noticed too late causes crashes, so make sure other drivers can see you. Remember: stalled and seen.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After a breakdown, make sure other drivers can see you and your vehicle, since crashes happen when a stalled car is noticed too late.

question.text: What should you do first when your vehicle has trouble, and how do you report it?

answer.text: With vehicle trouble, get off the road and away from traffic if at all possible, and turn on your emergency flashers.

teaching.text: Get off the road and away from traffic if at all possible, turn on your flashers, and report the breakdown by radio or phone. Remember: off the road, flashers on.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With vehicle trouble, get off the road and away from traffic if at all possible, and turn on your emergency flashers.

question.text: If you cannot leave the roadway, where should you stop?

answer.text: If you cannot leave the roadway, stop where others can clearly see you, not just past a hill crest or around a curve.

teaching.text: If you cannot leave the roadway, stop where others can clearly see you, not just past a hill crest or around a curve. Remember: not past crests or curves.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you cannot leave the roadway, stop where others can clearly see you, not just past a hill crest or around a curve.

question.text: Where do you set emergency flares, and why?

answer.text: Set emergency flares behind a disabled vehicle to warn drivers to change lanes.

teaching.text: Flares set behind a disabled vehicle warn drivers to change lanes before they reach it. Remember: flares behind.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Set emergency flares behind a disabled vehicle to warn drivers to change lanes.

question.text: Where should you never stand or change a tire, and how do you signal trouble?

answer.text: Never stand in the roadway or change a tire from inside a traffic lane; signal trouble by lifting the hood or tying a white cloth to the antenna, side mirror or door handle.

teaching.text: Never stand in the roadway or change a tire from a traffic lane; signal with the hood or a white cloth instead. Remember: never in the lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never stand in the roadway or change a tire from inside a traffic lane; signal trouble by lifting the hood or tying a white cloth to the antenna, side mirror or door handle.

question.text: Besides the antenna, where else can you tie a white cloth after a breakdown?

answer.text: The breakdown page adds the side mirror and door handle as places to tie a white cloth, beyond the antenna.

teaching.text: Besides the antenna, the white cloth can go on the side mirror or a door handle. Remember: mirror or door handle.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The breakdown page adds the side mirror and door handle as places to tie a white cloth, beyond the antenna.

hooks_spoken: Keep your eyes moving, and pull off the road before you study a map.
On one lane each way drive right and cross the center line only to pass safely; on wider highways keep right except to pass, make room or turn left.
Watch the speedometer, use the left lane for passing and never pass on the shoulder.
